articles.title: Five tasting menus under 40 euros that prove Madrid's mid-range dining scene is thriving
articles.excerpt: A new wave of small kitchens is closing the gap between casual dining and serious cooking.
articles.author: pablo-uria
articles.imageCaption: A plated dish from one of the featured kitchens | EP
content: A new wave of small, chef-owned kitchens is closing the gap between casual dining and serious cooking in the capital, with several offering full tasting menus for under 40 euros.
Industry figures say the trend reflects both rising costs at the top end of the market and a generation of chefs prioritising accessibility over spectacle.
Reservations at several of the featured spots are already booked out for weeks.

articles.title: Vermouth bars are making a comeback in Spain's mid-sized cities
articles.excerpt: What used to be a Sunday-before-lunch ritual is turning into an all-week draw for younger drinkers.
articles.author: pablo-uria
articles.imageCaption: A glass of vermouth served with an olive garnish | EP
content: Vermouth bars, long associated with a Sunday-before-lunch ritual in Spain's larger cities, are opening in growing numbers in mid-sized cities as well.
Owners say the format's low overhead and simple menu make it an easier bet than a full restaurant, while younger drinkers are treating it as a weeknight destination rather than a weekend one.
Several bars in the wave have added house-made vermouths to differentiate themselves from supermarket brands.

articles.title: Olive oil prices ease as producers report a stronger harvest outlook
articles.excerpt: After two difficult years, growers say rainfall this spring has meaningfully improved yield forecasts.
articles.author: sofia-marin
articles.imageCaption: Olives ready for harvest on a grove | EP
content: Olive oil prices have started to ease at wholesale level as producers report a stronger harvest outlook than in the previous two seasons.
Growers point to more favourable rainfall this spring as the main driver, after prolonged drought had pushed yields to historic lows and driven retail prices sharply higher.
Analysts caution that prices are unlikely to return to pre-drought levels this year, even if the improved forecast holds through the autumn harvest.

articles.title: Chefs are trading 12-course tasting menus for shorter, faster formats
articles.excerpt: Diners increasingly want a memorable meal without the three-hour commitment, kitchens say.
articles.author: pablo-uria
articles.imageCaption: A chef plating a dish in an open kitchen | EP
content: A number of well-regarded kitchens are shortening their tasting menus, trading the once-standard 12-course format for six or seven courses served over roughly ninety minutes.
Chefs say the shift responds to diners who want a memorable meal without committing an entire evening, particularly on weeknights.
Several restaurants report the shorter format has also let them turn tables twice in a service, improving margins without raising prices.

articles.title: Neighbourhood food markets see a revival as small vendors return
articles.excerpt: After years of decline, several municipal markets report their first fully-let vendor stalls in over a decade.
articles.author: sofia-marin
articles.imageCaption: Fresh produce stalls inside a municipal market | EP
content: Several municipal food markets are reporting their first fully-let vendor stalls in more than a decade, reversing a long decline driven by the rise of supermarkets and online grocery delivery.
Local authorities in a handful of cities credit reduced rents and small-business grants aimed at keeping markets viable as anchors for surrounding neighbourhoods.
Vendors say demand has been strongest for specialty goods that are harder to find in large chains, from artisanal cheese to regional produce.
